unit.title: I come from…
unit.communicativeGoal: Describe one's own and other people's origins by talking about countries and nationalities.
unit.competency: Use basic grammar, vocabulary, and phrases for countries and nationalities in short spoken and written exchanges.
prerequisites: Unit 1 subject pronouns and the verb to be
The distinction between a person, a country, and a nationality
languageTargets: country names: Japan, Peru, the USA, Australia, the Netherlands
nationalities: Japanese, Peruvian, American, Australian, Dutch
be from + country: I am from Spain.
come from + country: They come from Venezuela.
Where are you from? / Where do you come from?
do/does questions with the base verb come
country and nationality names begin with capital letters

sequence.title: Lee dos perfiles
sequence.objective: Read country, nationality, family-origin, and language facts, then distinguish what is stated about a person from what is stated about their family.
sequence.instruction: Lee el texto y elige la respuesta que aparece en el texto. No infieras el origen de una persona si la frase solo describe a sus padres.
sequence.readingText: Jenny is from the USA, so she is American. She was born in San Antonio, Texas. Her parents are Mexican; they come from Monterrey. Jenny speaks English, and she speaks Spanish too because her parents speak Spanish. Jenny's boyfriend is Takaishi; he is American too, but his parents are from Japan. He speaks English and Japanese.

sequence.title: Intercambia dos perfiles
sequence.objective: Demonstrate that the learner can identify and communicate who is from where, state a nationality, and answer a follow-up question.
sequence.instruction: Crea dos perfiles ficticios y haz un intercambio. Para cada persona incluye país y nacionalidad; luego responde una pregunta de seguimiento.

requiredOutput: Two fictional profiles, each with a person/name, country, and nationality
One spoken introduction for each profile
One follow-up question and answer about country, nationality, or language
A clarification turn when the listener does not understand a country
modelExchange: This is Nina. She is from Japan. She is Japanese.
task.sourceBoundary: Use fictitious profiles or the profile bank. Do not present an unverified audio speaker's identity as a new fact.

runtimeMappingGuidance.choiceScenes: Project each authored closed item to a native multiple_choice block with items[{id,question,options[{id,text}],correctOptionId,explanation}]. Preserve one click/keyboard check and a single Comprobar-to-Siguiente control.
runtimeMappingGuidance.teachScenes: Each scene carries learner-facing runtimeBlocks with concise Spanish directions, English examples or task language, and teaching tables only when they support the lesson. Do not place answer-revealing evidence tables before a question.
runtimeMappingGuidance.audioScenes: Each original audio row appears once as a native audio block with its exact URL and sourceID. Scene 4 is a replay reference to scene 2, not a second original row. Grade only exact transcriptEvidence; exploratory audio notes remain essay/open response with doNotAutoGrade.
runtimeMappingGuidance.productionScenes: Rehearsal and final speaking use native recording blocks with explicit individual and teacher learningModes, time limits, rubric metadata, and aiGrading:false. The optional 30–50 word extension uses native essay fields.
runtimeMappingGuidance.sourceRetention: Do not replace sourceIDs with runtime IDs. New scene IDs are presentation containers; attempts and progress resolve through the original sourceIDs in studentHistory.

implementationNotes.teachBeforeTest: Scenes 01–03 teach/activate; scene 04 checks three explicit audio quotations; scene 05 teaches grammar; scene 06 checks five controlled forms; scene 07 teaches through reading and checks five explicit evidence items; scene 08 checks only three safe transcript facts and leaves the ambiguous clause ungraded; scene 09 consolidates; scenes 10–11 move to open communication.
implementationNotes.audioPolicy: Audio1 country/language checks use quoted transcript evidence and avoid inferred speaker-name mapping. Audio2 grades only explicit Venezuela, American dad, and visit-him evidence; the unclear subject in 'they come from Venezuela' is preserved as an ambiguity note and never keyed.
implementationNotes.historyPolicy: Runtime translation retains sourceIDs on every derived scene, preserves all 31 original row IDs in the student history ledger, and leaves teacher notes out of the learner route.
implementationNotes.languagePolicy: Spanish is used for directions, feedback, and teacher notes. English is used for learning content, target forms, questions, answer choices, and model exchanges.
implementationNotes.visualPolicy: Use the unique existing approved backgroundAsset recorded per scene with its complete painterly environment. Keep navy serif hierarchy, legible protected text, one cobalt primary action, click/keyboard checking, and recognizable mobile navigation.
